item.title: French far-left candidate Mélenchon opens door to alliance with rival Greens candidate
item.description: French far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon opened the door to an alliance with France's Greens on Thursday after their presidential candidate Marine Tondelier said she was ready to "work on a coalition around" the veteran leftist. Tondelier's overture has further boosted Mélenchon's campaign for the Élysée Palace – and angered moderates on the centre-left.

item.title: Kenyan marathon champion banned for doping
item.description: In tonight's edition, Kenyan athletics superstar and reigning marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir is banned for three years for doping. Also, South African judges leave the courtroom behind and tour a repatriation centre before handing down judgment in 33 emergency asylum applications. And Ghana's presidency has a new jet, but critics of the ruling party are not on board.

item.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv kill one, damage Dutch and Austrian embassies
item.description: A wave of daytime Russian strikes on Kyiv on Thursday killed one person and damaged a historic cathedral as well as the embassies of Austria and the Netherlands. Loud explosions erupted across the Ukraine capital throughout the day as the leaders of Russia, China and the United States held a historic meeting in China that put Russia's President Vladimir Putin in international spotlight. FRANCE 24's Laurent Berstecher reports.

item.title: 'We're seeing in real time the effects that AI is going to have on cybersecurity', expert says
item.description: FRANCE 24's Monte Francis speaks with Dr. R. David Edelman, Senior Fellow at the Brookings Institution, also former Director for Cybersecurity on the National Security Council under the Obama administration. He explains that the latest spate of network outages shows "in real time the effects that AI is going to have on cybersecurity" adding that "the one thing that's tying most of these outages together is that companies and institutions are racing to patch a system that's been identified as vulnerable, and they're patching what themselves are pretty creaky digital systems".

item.title: Kushner says Trump 'open' to extend NATO mutual defense-type clause to Ukraine
item.description: US envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday that President Donald Trump was open to extending to Ukraine a security guarantee similar to NATO's mutual defense clause, but stressed that Washington has to protect its interests too. The comments came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz qualified the summit between the presidents of the United States, Russia and China as a "photo op". FRANCE 24's international affairs commentator Douglas Herbert explains.
